newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilgener mulls early start-up of plant.
newsitem.headline: Chilgener mulls early start-up of plant.

text.p: Chile's second largest power generator Chilgener said it is studying bringing forward the start-up of its gas-fired Nueva Renca power plant to ease the power shortage caused by this year's drought.
"We are evaluating advancing the start-up of Nueva Renca," general manager Juan Antonio Guzman told reporters.
He declined to say when Nueva Renca, which is due to come online in early November, could start generating power.
If it does begin early, the plant will initially produce 220 megawatts of power, less than its top capacity of 370 megawatts, he said.

Chile announced on Monday emergency measures, including a five percent reduction in power voltage, to cut consumption of electricity. Output from hydroelectric generators, which account for most of Chile's power, has been slashed in recent months by the drought.
A long-term solution to the problem is to ensure power generation is more evenly balanced between hydroelectric and thermal generators, said Guzman.
In years of normal rainfall, thermal generators produce 15 percent of the needs of Chile's central grid, with the rest coming from hydro-electric plants, government officials said recently.
But as a result of the drought, thermal generators are producing 50 percent of the power supplied to the central grid, the officials said.
